articles.title: Lei Hnuaia Hrui Inzawm: Sik leh Sa Inthlak Karah Lei Ṭha Siamthar Dan

author.name: Dr. Lalhmingmawii Vance
author.bio: Leilung nung (rhizosphere biome), thing phur zungzawng (fungal-bacterial ratios), leh leitha vawn ngheh dan zirchiangtu.

comments.content: Lei let lova crimson clover phah kan hman atang khan July thla ro lai pawhin kan leilung hian tui a chelh rei em em a, thlai an thi ve mai mai tawh lo.
AMF leh thlai zung thawhhona hi a pawimawh hle mai. Chemical phosphorus fertilizer tam lutuk hian he fungi hi a tihchingpen theih dan zirtirna a awm em?

articles.content:
## Kan Ke Hnuai Leilung Nung Chanchin

Kum sawm ruk liamta chhung khan leilung hi bungrua leh thing remkhawm ang maiah ngaiin chemical fertilizer chi hrang hrang leh damdawi hman khawlohnain kan tichhe hle a. Leilung kan let chiam hian leilung nungcha pawimawh em em **Arbuscular Mycorrhizal Fungi (AMF)** zung tam tak kan ti chat bawk thin.

He fungi hrui inzawmna tello chuan leilungin tui a chelh theihna (sponge ang leilung) a bo va, ruah a surin lei ṭha a luang ral a, khaw ro deuh hlekin lei a khi phutin thlai an thi thuai thin a ni.

> *"Leilung hrisel ṭha kut khat chhung lek pawh hian khawvel mihring zawng zawng awm tawh zat aia tam leilung nungcha te tak te an cheng a ni. Thlai chauh kan enkawl lo, leilung rilpui kan chawm a ni."*
> — **Dr. Lalhmingmawii Vance**, Institute for Regenerative Agriculture

---

### Mycorrhizae leh Thlai Zung Thawhhona

Thlai zung hian AMF fungi nen thawhhona ropui tak an nei a:

1. **Thlai Thlum Pek:** Thlaiin ni zung atanga chaw (carbon sugar) a siam za zela 10 atanga 30 chu thlai zung kaltlangin he fungi hian a hmu thin.
2. **Lei Chaw & Tui Laklet:** Fungi zung (hyphae) te tak te hian thlai zung thlen phak loh leilung thuk tak atangin phosphorus, zinc, copper leh tui chu thlai tan a la chhuak thung.
3. **Glomalin Siamna:** He fungi hian *Glomalin* an tih leilung char tak tak leh tui tichemin bel khawmtu a siam chhuak a, lei tuihawk lakah a vawng him bawk.

| Leilung Tehna | Chemical & Lei Let Nasat | Leilung Nung & Fungi Enkawl | Hmasawnna Hmuhchhuah |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Tui Hip Luh Chak Lam** | Darkarah inch 0.8 | Darkarah inch 6.4 | **Za zela 700-in a chak zawk** |
| **Fungi Hriselna Zat** | 22 µg/g leilung | 385 µg/g leilung | **A let 17.5-in a tam zawk** |
| **Glomalin Khawlkhawm** | 1.1 mg/g | 6.8 mg/g | **Lei chim lakah a him** |
| **Phosphorus Thlaiin a Hman** | Chemical DAP a ngai | Fungi-in amahin a phel darh | **Senso za zela 40-60 a tlem** |

---

### Leilung Fungi Tiharh Chhuak Tura Hmalak Dan

Leilung siamṭha tur hian sum tam tak sen a ngai lo; a hnah phah leh a zung enkawl a tawk em em a ni:

```
LEI TIHṬHATNA KAWNGPUI PALI:
[Pillar 1: Lei Let Chiamloh]       -> Lei chhuat vawng hle hle rawh
[Pillar 2: Thlai Hring Phah Reng]  -> Thlai lak hmain hnah phah thlai theh rawh
[Pillar 3: Chemical Tihhniam]      -> Chemical fertilizer za zela 25-in tlem telh telh rawh
[Pillar 4: Lei Lum Lutuk Venna]     -> Lei chunglang hnim rovin khuh reng rawh
```

#### 1. Hnah Phah Thlai (Cover Crops)
Thlai lak zawhin lei ruak ringawtin dah suh. Thlai chi hrang hrang pawlh la:
- **Be Chi (Legumes):** Boruak atangin leitha (nitrogen) leilungah an hip lut.
- **Zung Thuk Nei Chi (Radish / Chicory):** Leilung sak lutuk kawr thuk tak an verh tlang.
- **Hnim Hrui Nei Chi (Cereal Rye):** Fungi zung inzarpharna tur zau tak an pe.

#### 2. Biochar Hmanga Zung Venhim
Thlai ṭha phun dawnin meihawl leitha atana siam **Biochar** leiah pawlh rawh. Biochar hian tuibur te tak te ang maiin fungi te tan tui a chelh a, nungcha sual lakah a humhim bawk a ni.

---

### Loneitute Sum Hmuh Dan Hmasawnna
He leilung nung enkawl dan hian:
- Tractor leh leilung thawh hahna senso nasa takin a tihniam.
- Khaw ro lai kar thum (ni 21) chhung pawhin thlai an vuai lova, hring dupin an awm thei.
- Thlai thar hriselna leh a thlum dan (protein content) a sang zawk bawk.

articles.title: Tui Far Fawn Hman Dan Fing: Sensor leh LoRaWAN Hmanga Tui Sen Ral Za zela 44 Tihtlem Dan

author.name: Marcus Thorne
author.bio: Lo neihna atana khawl changkang, LoRaWAN wireless sensor, leh drone hmanga thlai hriselna enfiah dan thiam bik.

comments.content: Thlai zung bulah sensor kan dah a, thlai hian kan rin aia tlem tui a mamawh tih kan hria. Thei thlum dan leh hriselna a sang sawt hle.

articles.content:
## Sana Rinchhana Tui Pek A Tawk Tawh Lo

Kan huanah tui pek nan sana (timer) ngawt kan hmang thin a, ruah sur lai pawhin tui a kal a, a nih loh leh lei chhungril ro laiin a chunglang chauh a huh thin. Thlai hnah a vuai hnu chauhva tui kan pek hian thlai rah leh puitlin theihna a chhiat phah hman tawh thin a ni.

Tui a tlem tial tial lai hian leilung ro dan teh thiam sensor hmanga **thlai mamawh tawk chiah tui pek (precision irrigation)** a hun ta hle.

---

### LoRaWAN Wireless Telemetry Hman Dan

Huan kil khatah phone network a awm loh pawhin, **LoRaWAN (Long Range Wireless)** radio band hmangin kilometer 12 bial chhung sensor-te hian tui pekna khawl an be tlang thei a ni.

```
TUI PEK KHAWL INZAWN DAN:
[Huan Sensor Node] --(LoRa Radio)--> [Solar Gateway Khawl]
                                            |
                                      (Sim Card / Wi-Fi)
                                            v
[Phone / Local Controller] <--(Automated Trigger)-- [Tui Valve Hawngtu Khawl]
```

#### Huan Sensor Pawimawh Chite:
1. **Watermark Matric Potential Sensor:** Leilungin tui a chelh beh tlat dan leh thlai zungin tui a hip theih dan tehna (kPa).
2. **Thuk Lam Chhiarna Sensor (15cm, 45cm, 90cm):** Tui a liam thuk lutuk em tih leh leitha a tlen fai em tih hriatna.
3. **Thlai Hnah Lum Lam Tehna (Canopy Infrared):** Thlai hnah a lum chuan tui a khawm tawh lo tih hriatna a ni.

---

### Leilung Chi Hrang Hrang Tana Tui Pek Hun
| Leilung Chi | A Huh Ṭha Lai | Tui Pek Hun Chiah | A Ro Lutuk Tawh |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Tiau Lei (Sand)** | 5 – 10 kPa | **25 – 35 kPa** | > 45 kPa |
| **Leilung Pangngai (Sandy Loam)** | 10 – 20 kPa | **40 – 50 kPa** | > 70 kPa |
| **Hlum Lei (Silt Clay)** | 20 – 30 kPa | **60 – 75 kPa** | > 100 kPa |
| **Leitha Tam Hlum (Heavy Clay)** | 25 – 35 kPa | **80 – 95 kPa** | > 120 kPa |

---

### Sum Senso Tlem Dan
- **Current / Diesel Senso:** Zan lamah leilungin tui a hip ṭhat lai chauhva tui pek anih avangin za zela 38.4-in electric senso a tlahniam.
- **Leitha Luang Ral Tur Venna:** Tui a liam lutuk loh avangin chemical leitha a tlen bo lo.
- **Khawl Senso Hmuhlet Leh:** Tui leh khawl hmanna senso hi thla 8 chhung lekin tui man leh thlai thar tam atangin a luh let leh nghal a ni.

articles.title: Silvopasture: Thing Phun, Hnim Hring Leh Ran Vulh Kawp Dan Ṭha
articles.category: Ran Vulh leh Thing Phun Kawp

author.name: Priya Nair
author.bio: Thing lian hlimhnuaia ran vulh, thlai leh theihuan chin kawp (multi-strata agroforestry) zirchiangtu.

articles.content:
## Thing Phun Leh Ran Vulh Kar Thu

Hmanlai atangin ram ngaw leh ran vulh hi inhmelma ang maiin an ngai thin a: loneitute chuan thing an kit fai vek a, thing enkawltute chuan ran an um bo thin.

Mahse **Silvopasture** chuan he ngaihdan hi a thlak thawk a ni: thing lian, ran chaw hnim tha, leh ran vulh kawpin ram hmun khatah hlawkna thaphat (thingfak, hnim, leh ran sa/hnute) a siam chhuak thei a ni.

---

### Silvopasture Chhawng Thumte
```
SILVOPASTURE CHHAWNGTE:
[Chhawng Chungnung] -> Thing hlim leh thei kung (Chestnut / Walnut / Thingfak)
[Chhawng Laifang]    -> Ran chaw hnah tha (Leucaena / Tagasaste / Hazelnut)
[Chhawng Hnuailang]  -> Hnim hring chaw ṭha (Clover / Orchardgrass / Chicory)
[Ran Vulhte]         -> Bawng, Beram, Vawk tlan kual thin
```

#### 1. Ran Lum Lutuk Laka Venhimna
Bawng leh ran hian khawlum lutuk (27°C aia sang) an tuar lo em em a, hnute pek a tlem a, an thau thei thin lo. Thing hlim hnuaiah erawh:
- Boruak lum lam chu **4°C atanga 7°C-in a vawt zawk**.
- Leilung lum lutuk lakah a vawng him a, leilung nungchate an dam khawchhuak thei.
- Ran thau chak lam a tla tlahniam ve lo.

---

### Thing Chi Thlan Dan & Hlawkna
| Thing Chi | Than Chak Lam | Hlawkna Hmasa | Hlawkna Dang |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Honey Locust** | Kum 8-12 | Fencing ban, thingfak | A rah hian thlum leh protein tam tak a pai |
| **Chestnut** | Kum 4-6 | A rah hralh theih | Thingzar hlim nuam tak |
| **Black Walnut** | Kum 30-45 | Thingfak to tak | A hnuai hnim a ti thi ve lo |
| **Oak (Thang)** | Kum rei | Thingfak chang | A rah hi vawk chaw tana ṭha tak a ni |

---

### Ran Vahkual Dan (Rotational Grazing)
Ran chu hmun khatah dah reng tur a ni lo. Solar electric fence te tak te hmangin ni tin emaw kar tin hmun tharah sawn zel tur:
1. **A thum a chhe khat:** Ranin hnim za zela 33 an ei a, 33 an rap bet a, 33 a chawr leh nan an kalsan thin.
2. **Chawlh Hahtdam Tir:** Ram chu ni 45 atanga 90 chhung chawlh hahdam tir leh thin tur a ni.

He hian leilung nung a ti pung a, thingzung pawh a tichhe lova, leitha nasa takin a vawng reng thin a ni.

articles.title: Thei Huan Changkan Dan: Thlai Phun Khawm (High-Density) leh Rannung Hrik Ven Dan

author.name: David Lalthanpuia
author.bio: Polyhouse chhung thlai chin, thei chi ṭha thlan, leh rannung laka thlai venhimna damdawi tel lova kalpui thiam.

articles.content:
## Thei Huan Siam Dan Thlak A Hun Ta

Hmanlai chuan thei kung hi hla tak takah phun a ni a, a kung a lian lutuk a, a hnuailang zarah ni zung a thleng lo va, a rah lawh dawnin harsa takin lawn a ngai thin.

Tuna theihuan enkawl dan thar **2D Planar Fruiting Wall** ah chuan:

---

### Trellis Wire Hmanga Thlai Phun Khawm
Thlai zung te chi (dwarf rootstock) hmangin thir hruiah thei zarte chu bang ang maia thlep felin enkawl a ni:
- Hektare khatah thei kung 200 chauh phun thin kha **2,500 atanga 3,500** thleng phun theih a ni ta.
- Thei rah za zela 92-in ni zung tawk chiah an dawng a, a rawng leh a thlum a rualkhai em em.
- Rah lawh a awlsam a, hlawhfa lak hah a tlem sawt.

```
2D PLANAR FRUITING WALL TRELLIS:
[Hrui 4: 2.8m] ====== Thei Zar ====== Thei Zar ======
[Hrui 3: 2.1m] ====== Thei Zar ====== Thei Zar ======
[Hrui 2: 1.4m] ====== Thei Zar ====== Thei Zar ======
[Hrui 1: 0.7m] ====== A Kung Zung ==== A Kung Zung ====
```

---

### Damdawi Tur Tel Lova Rannung Ven Dan
1. **Pheromone Rim Hmanga Hrik Hruai Bo:** Rannung nu rim ang chiah solar dispenser hmangin tlaiah chhuah a ni a, rannung pate chuan a nute an zawng hmu thei lo va, chi an thlah thei lo.
2. **Rannung Ṭhate Vulh:** Huan kiltirah pangpar rimtui (sweet alyssum) chin a ni a, he hian hrik eitu rulhut leh vate a ko khawm a, thei tichhe theitu hrik an ei zo thin.

Kum 2-na lekah thei thar a tan theih avangin loneitute tan sum senso laklet a chak em em a ni.

articles.title: Biochar: Thlai Rohnah Hal Ruak Lova Meihawl Ṭhaa Chantir leh Lei Tihṭhat Nan Hman Dan

author.name: Dr. Lalhmingmawii Vance
author.bio: Leilung nung (rhizosphere biome), thing phur zungzawng (fungal-bacterial ratios), leh leitha vawn ngheh dan zirchiangtu.

articles.content:
## Thing Ro Hal Ruak Aiin: Meihawl Ropui Biochar

Fur leh thlasikah thing zar ro, buh fawng, leh thlai hnawmte hal liam mai kan ching a. He hian boruak a ti chhe mai bakah leitha tur tam tak a hal ral thin a ni.

Boruak (oxygen) tlem te chauh luh theihna kilnah 450°C atanga 650°C-a kan ur hian **Biochar (Meihawl Leitha)** ah a chang a, he meihawl hian kum sangkhat (1,000) dawn leilungah leitha a vawng reng thei a ni.

---

### Biochar Mawina Leh Ṭhatna
Biochar gram khat lek pawh hian khua chhung zau zawng (250-450 sq. meters) khawpa zau tuibur te tak te a pai a.

> *"Biochar hi a thara leiah theh nghal ngawt chi a ni lo; sponge ro tak tui chhunga dah ang maiin thlai tana tui leh leitha a hip fai vek thei. Hman hmain leitha (compost) leh ek tuiah kar hnih chhung chiah phawt tur a ni."*
> — **Loneitu Field Note**

---

### Hman Tura Siam Dan:
1. **Sawh Sawm:** Biochar chu 2mm atanga 6mm vel leka tein sawk sawm rawh.
2. **Compost Nen Pawlh:** Biochar hlawm khat leh leitha (compost) hlawm li pawlh rawh.
3. **Chiah Huh:** Tui leh rul leitha tuiah ni 14 chhung chiah huh rawh.
4. **Leiah Pawlh:** Thlai phun dawnin a zung bul leiah pawlh la, i damchhungin a ṭhatna a bo tawh lovang.

articles.title: Ni Zung Ni Hnuaia Thlai Vawn Vawhna (Solar Cold Storage): Loneitute Hlawkna Tihpun Dan

author.name: Marcus Thorne
author.bio: Lo neihna atana khawl changkang, LoRaWAN wireless sensor, leh drone hmanga thlai hriselna enfiah dan thiam bik.

articles.content:
## Thlai Chhe Ral Venhimna

Thingtlâng hmun hla tak takah kan thlai thar, thei, leh thlai hring za zela 40 vel chu bazar a thlen hmain a chhe ral thin a. Current a that tawk loh avangin loneituten an thlai an hralh hmanhmawh a, a man tlawm te tein dawrkai an hralh luih luih thin a ni.

He harsatna sut kian nan **Ni Zung Hmanga Thlai Vawn Vawhna (Solar Cold Storage)** a lo chhuak ta.

---

### Phase-Change Material (PCM) Hman Dan
Battery to lutuk hman a ngai lova, chhunah ni zung chakna hmangin vûr tlang (PCM Salt Hydrate) an ti khal a, zanah ni a lan loh pawhin he vûr tlang hian darkar 36 atanga 48 chhung room vawt tak (4°C) a vawng reng thei a ni.

```
SOLAR COLD STORAGE KAL DAN:
[Solar Plate (5kW - 10kW)]
          | (Chhun ni zung hmangin)
          v
[Compressor Khawl]
          |
          +---> [Thlai dahna pindan chu 4°C-ah a ti vawt]
          |
          +---> [PCM Tui chu -3°C-ah vurah a chantir]
                     |
(Zanah: Ni a tla, khawl a thi)
                     v
[Vur khal tui zawngin a vawh a chhuah a, thlai a vawng him reng]
```

---

### Loneitute Sum Hmuh Dan Hmasawnna
Loneitu inzawmkhawm ten he cold storage an neih hian:
- **Thlai Hring:** Antam, zikhlum, leh hmarcha chu ni 2 chauh hring thin kha **ni 21 chhung** thar em emin an vawng vawt thei.
- **Hralh Hun Thlan Thiam:** Bazarah thlai a tam laiin an hralh buai lo va, thlai tlem lai leh man to lai takah an hralh chauh thin.
- **Hlawkna:** Loneitu chhungkuate sum hmuh za zela **31.4-in a pung nghal a ni**.

**2. Comprehensive Operational and Administrative Profile of Mizo Farm Solutions**
1. Executive Summary and Legal Identity
Mizo Farm Solutions is a registered society operating primarily in Mizoram, committed to the modernization, sustainability, and socio-economic strengthening of the agricultural and rural development sectors. Although the society is a young institution with four years of collective operational presence, it is led and supported by members who bring extensive individual knowledge, field exposure, technical qualifications, and sectoral experience. This combination enables the society to function with both youthful institutional energy and mature professional capability. Legally recognized by the Government of Mizoram, the society holds a Certificate of Registration under the Mizoram Societies Registration Act, 2005 (Act No. 13 of 2005). The official Registration Number assigned to the organization is MSR 1863 of 07.04.2026, which was formally granted on April 7, 2026, at Aizawl by the Registrar of Firms & Societies. All provisions of the Mizoram Societies Registration Act, 2005, are fully applicable to the operations and legal proceedings of this society.

**Recent Accolades: Mizoram Grand Challenge**
Demonstrating excellence in strategic planning and innovation, Mizo Farm Solutions was recently awarded the Third Prize in the prestigious Mizoram Grand Challenge. Competing in the Open Category, the society secured a ₹50,000 award for its comprehensive and actionable project pitch focused on the "establishment of robust post-harvest infrastructure." This achievement highlights the organization's capability to devise systemic solutions for deep-rooted agricultural challenges within the state.
2. Primary Development Priorities and NGO Convergence
Beyond its stated technological objectives, the absolute core priority of Mizo Farm Solutions is the socio-economic upliftment of rural youth, the empowerment of women, and comprehensive rural development. To actively execute these priorities at the grassroots level, Mizo Farm Solutions has successfully established strategic operational convergences with Cod Nerc and the Impulse NGO Network. Through these collaborative partnerships, the society is driving tangible rural development projects, which prominently include:
•	The large-scale construction of Green Houses to promote controlled micro-climate farming.
•	The systematic and widespread distribution of high-quality agricultural seedlings to rural farmers.
•	The initiation of community-level vermicompost production to support organic farming transitions.
•	Specialized drives for citrus seedling production, aimed at generating long-term, sustainable livelihood opportunities for indigenous communities.
3. Core Operational Activities
Mizo Farm Solutions is actively engaged in transforming the agricultural landscape of Mizoram. The work currently being done by the society includes:
•	Implementing Precision Agriculture via AI & IoT: The organization expertise in deploying Artificial Intelligence and Internet of Things (IoT) sensors to revolutionize traditional farming. This enables real-time monitoring of soil moisture, crop health, and weather, facilitating data-driven decisions that optimize resources and maximize yields. 
•	Executing Farm Mechanization and Automation: To reduce physical drudgery and labor costs, the society can provide access to modern machinery—such as drones for spraying, automated harvesters, and laser land levellers—making technology accessible to smallholder farmers through shared ownership models. 
•	Advancing Organic and Natural Farming: Mizo Farm Solutions is specialize facilitating the certification and cultivation of chemical-free produce, utilizing bio-fertilizers and natural farming techniques to restore soil health and cater to global organic demands. 
•	Executing Integrated Crop Management (ICM): The society can implement holistic farm management, balancing chemical fertilizers with organic manure (INM), utilizing biological controls alongside judicious chemical use (IPM), and deploying proactive disease forecasting (IDM). 
•	Developing Protected Cultivation Infrastructure: The organization expertise in establishing and managing modern housing facilities like polyhouses, net houses, and glasshouses, enabling the year-round cultivation of high-value horticulture and floriculture crops. 
•	Managing Post-Harvest Infrastructure: To drastically reduce post-harvest losses, the society can construct and manages scientific warehousing and cold storage chains, allowing farmers to store perishables and sell during favorable market conditions. 
•	Facilitating Value Addition and Food Processing: Mizo Farm Solutions can set up primary and secondary processing units for grading, sorting, packaging, and manufacturing, converting raw produce into shelf-stable consumer products. 
•	Supplying Strategic Agri-Inputs: The organization functions as a reliable expert in node for high-quality, certified seeds, fertilizers, and agrochemicals, ensuring they are used scientifically to prevent soil degradation. 
•	Strengthening Market Linkages: By utilizing digital e-marketing platforms and establishing efficient logistics, the society can connect farmers directly to retailers and consumers, effectively eliminating intermediaries. 
•	Conducting Capacity Building: Acting as a centre of learning, the society conducts regular training, demonstrations, and workshops on modern scientific methods and financial literacy to empower youth as Agri-entrepreneurs. 
4. Comprehensive Rural Development: 
Off-Farm and Allied Initiatives
Recognizing that true rural prosperity requires livelihood diversification beyond traditional agriculture, Mizo Farm Solutions and its members collectively execute a robust portfolio of off-farm and non-farm activities. These initiatives are designed to generate parallel income streams, reduce dependency on seasonal harvests, and build socio-economic resilience:
•	Small-Scale Manufacturing & Cottage Industries: The members actively promote indigenous manufacturing at the village level. This includes the establishment of handloom weaving clusters, tailoring units, and the production of traditional artisanal crafts, directly creating non-farm employment for rural women.
•	Agro-Processing & Local Value Addition: Beyond raw crop sales, members facilitate secondary food processing enterprises. This involves training communities in pickle making, fruit preservation, spice grinding, and eco-friendly packaging, thereby converting local produce into high-margin consumer goods.
•	Micro-Enterprise and Rural Trading: The members provide financial literacy and mentorship to rural youth to help them establish small-scale retail shops, rural supply stores, and community service centres.
•	Digital Literacy and Rural Services: Bridging the digital divide, the member runs capacity-building programs to train rural youth in computer operations, desktop publishing, and basic IT services, enabling them to secure employment in the growing rural service sector.
•	Rural Logistics and Supply Chain Management: Utilizing internal expertise, the society is involved in organizing and optimizing rural transportation networks. This ensures that remote farmers have reliable logistical pathways to transport their goods to urban markets efficiently.
•	Allied Animal Husbandry: Though closely linked to farming, the society actively supports the off-field establishment of dairy units, poultry farms, and piggery enterprises to ensure consistent, year-round household income.
**
5. Institutional Expertise and Sectoral Experience**
Mizo Farm Solutions is a four-year-old society strengthened by the accumulated professional experience of its members and technical personnel. While the society’s institutional journey is still developing, its operational capacity is built on the proven field knowledge, academic qualifications, practical implementation experience, and community engagement history of its members. This allows the society to present itself credibly as an emerging institution with a strong human-resource foundation and clear development orientation.
Handloom, Handicrafts, and Artisanal Empowerment
Members associated with Mizo Farm Solutions possess extensive, deeply rooted experience in the local arts, crafts, and handloom sectors. Their individual expertise includes textile designing, traditional weaving, artisan training, and craft-based livelihood promotion. Through these member-led capabilities, the society is well positioned to support rural employment, preserve indigenous skills, and promote artisanal empowerment. Members have also been involved in guiding, employing, and training more than 200 villagers in handloom and craft techniques, contributing meaningfully to rural job creation and skill preservation.
Agriculture Extension and Field Implementation
The members of the organization bring more than a decade of individual field experience in agriculture and horticulture. Their professional backgrounds include work in coordination with NABARD and experience under Mizoram Government flagship schemes such as NLUP and FOCUS. The society benefits from members who have contributed to academic research, published research papers, received appreciation certificates from public authorities, and provided direct field-level guidance and training to farmers. This member-driven expertise strengthens the society’s ability to implement practical, farmer-oriented interventions with credibility and technical depth.
Engineering and Infrastructure Development
The technical personnel associated with the society provide strong civil and structural engineering capability, supported by more than five years of individual experience in design, construction, and infrastructure-related works. This expertise includes exposure to agricultural and municipal infrastructure, storm drain projects, RKVY-related initiatives, and other government and private development works. As a society, Mizo Farm Solutions draws on this technical capacity to plan and support infrastructure components in a professional and responsible manner.
Socio-Economic Development, Education, and Financial Management
Beyond technical farming, members of Mizo Farm Solutions bring more than 10 years of individual experience in educational campaigns, awareness programmes, farmer engagement, youth development, and rural community outreach. The society is also supported by members with practical experience in commercial sales, accounting, cooperative operations, and financial management. These combined strengths help ensure that its agricultural and rural development activities are backed by sound planning, responsible administration, and sustainable business thinking.








**7. Adequacy of infrastructure facilities of Mizo Farm Solutions, Champhai.**
•	Office of The Project Director, Mizo Farm Solutions, Champhai is located inside Champhai with separate building and administration at Jail Veng, Champhai.
•	High speed internet facility is provided in the office 24x7.
•	All prerequisites needed for an effective operation of an office is available in Mizo Farm Solutions office.
•	All the staff have been provided with a good quality laptop for executing desk work.
